extractedText: I thought my repairable Android phone would last 10 years—it lasted 3 months Credit: Bertel King / How-To Geek By Bertel King Published Jun 28, 2026, 10:15 AM EDT Bertel is a lifelong tech enthusiast with over a decade of experience writing thousands of articles about Android devices, Linux, and more. Before joining the How-To Geek team, Bertel wrote for the likes of MakeUseOf, MakeTechEasier, and Android Police—at the latter he wrote over 3,500 articles. He delights in helping others decide which tech to bring into their lives... and which tech to do without. Bertel graduated from the College of William and Mary in 2012 with degrees in History and Government. He has spent his entire career as a tech journalist covering Android, Linux, wearables, smart home devices, and more. Sign in to your How-To Geek account Add Us On Jump links Jump Links My Fairphone (Gen 6) can no longer charge My Fairphone is not alone My faith in this phone has been completely shattered follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap I loved my foldable Galaxy Z Fold, but I was so enamored by the idea of a repairable and open-source phone that I was willing to go back to a traditional slab in order to give this experiment a shot. So I bought the Murena Fairphone 6 with the idea that this would be a device I could preserve for many years to come. Then, out of the blue, this dream came to an end. My Fairphone (Gen 6) can no longer charge This is not the way I expected my phone to break The Fairphone (Gen 6) has nearly a dozen components that are user replaceable. I can swap out the battery, the camera lenses, the speakers, the USB port, and even the microphone. I've taken some of these parts out and put them back in myself. It's a satisfying feeling. Unfortunately, there are many parts of the Fairphone that can't be easily repaired, despite its perfect iFixit score. If you drop the phone and damage the frame, that's not something you can swap out. If your volume rocker or power button stop working, you will still need to send the phone in for repairs. Murena Fairphone (Gen. 6) Brand Murena Display 6.31 inches The Murena Fairphone (Gen. 6) is the perfect option to bring together privacy and sustainability. Powered by the /e/OS operating system, the Fairphone (Gen. 6) protects you and your data at all times, while at the same time protecting the planet. $750 at Murena Expand Collapse This is the situation I find myself in. One morning, I woke up to a low battery alert, but when I plugged in my phone, nothing happened. I tried many different chargers, a charging station, and even plugged my phone into my PC. Nothing worked. Since the Fairphone does not support wireless charging, this means the phone is effectively dead. My only option is to turn it off before it drains itself entirely. My Fairphone is not alone Others have found themselves with phones that have stopped working Credit: Bertel King / How-To Geek Shortly after I bought the Fairphone, I realized that I was taking a risk. Searching Reddit and the Fairphone forums, I saw there were quite a few customers with devices that no longer came on. There's an old and particularly lengthy thread filled with people talking about the possibility that their phone overheated while charging, damaging an aspect of the motherboard irreparably. There are many threads like this one, this one, and this one that mirror the situation I'm facing now. Those posts are from 2025, but the problem persists. Unfortunately, even if you're aware of the risk, the steps necessary to avoid this fate are unclear. Some customers recommend avoiding fast chargers, but if you read Fairphone's own recommendations, they suggest using a charger with a minimum of 30W. The Fairphone also has a setting to limit charging speeds, but some customers suspect they ran into issues precisely because of this option, so I felt it was probably safer for me to avoid it. In either case, this situation is quite unacceptable. I've been charging countless devices via both USB-C and microUSB for decades and have never had a device fail on me out of the blue. If a product isn't safely able to regulate its charging speed, that is a defect. My faith in this phone has been completely shattered How do I know this won't happen again? Credit: Bertel King / How-To Geek The downside of purchasing a device like the Fairphone in the US is that there is no local support. I can't simply walk into a repair shop and expect a same-day turnaround time like I sometimes can with an iPhone, a Galaxy phone, or a Pixel. This phone has to be mailed in. When I reached out to Murena about the issue, it was nearly a week before I got a response, and there has since been more days of back and forth over email.
